title: Integrality is insensitive to thickenings
statement: Let $i_S:S\to S'$ and $i_X:X\to X'$ be thickenings of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (closed immersions that are surjective on underlying spaces), and let $f':X'\to S'$ and $f:X\to S$ be morphisms with $f'\circ i_X=i_S\circ f$ (a morphism of thickenings $(X\subseteq X')\to(S\subseteq S')$; no cartesian or finite order hypothesis). Then $f$ is integral if and only if $f'$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. (Stacks proves it from: $f$ affine iff $f'$ affine (part (1), via the bijection of affine opens of a thickening, More on Morphisms 06AD), $f$ universally closed iff $f'$ universally closed (part (4), since $i_S$, $i_X$ are universal homeomorphisms, Morphisms 054M), and integral = affine + universally closed (Morphisms 01WM).)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZV (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms), part (5), with parts (1), (4) and the proof

proof.text: (Setup.) $i_S:S\to S'$ and $i_X:X\to X'$ are closed immersions that are surjective on underlying spaces [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], hence homeomorphisms onto $S'$, $X'$. By the closed-immersion clauses, $i_S$ and $i_X$ are separated, affine, integral and universally closed. Write $g:=f'\circ i_X=i_S\circ f:X\to S'$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 09ZV, first sentence (S→S', X→X' are universal homeomorphisms); the clauses used are Morphisms 01QU, 01SE, 035C, 01W5

proof.text: ($f'$ integral $\Rightarrow$ $f$ integral.) If $f'$ is integral, then $g=f'\circ i_X$ is integral as a composite of the integral morphisms $i_X$ (step 1) and $f'$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc (c),(e)]. So $i_S\circ f=g$ is integral and $i_S$ is separated (step 1); hence $f$ is integral by Morphisms 035D (2) [lem-weil-pbc-integral-of-comp-separated]. (Stacks derives this direction from (1), (4) and 01WM as for the converse; this argument is shorter and uses only 035D.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01WK (composition) and Lemma 035D (2); route of the direction written by the agent in place of 09ZV (1)+(4)

proof.text: (From now on $f$ integral. $f$ is affine and universally closed.) By Morphisms 01WM [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed], the integral morphism $f$ is affine and universally closed.

($f'$ universally closed: 09ZV (4), direction $f\Rightarrow f'$.) $g=i_S\circ f$ is universally closed as the composite of the universally closed morphisms $f$ (step 3) and $i_S$ (step 1) [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc (d),(f)]. Now $g=f'\circ i_X$ with $g$ universally closed and $i_X$ surjective [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]; by the image lemma [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] (Mathlib UniversallyClosed.of_comp_surjective) (with $p:=g$, the surjection $i_X:X\to X'$ and $q:=f'$, $q\circ i_X=p$) $f'$ is universally closed. (Stacks says (4) follows 'immediately' from $i_S$, $i_X$ being universal homeomorphisms; this is that argument written out.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 09ZV, sentences 1-2 (part (4))

proof.text: Affineness of f implies affineness of f′ by isAffineHom_of_thickenings, the affine-open reduction recorded in lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-morphism.
($f'$ integral.) By steps 4 and 5, $f'$ is affine and universally closed, hence integral by Morphisms 01WM [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed] ((2)⇒(1)). With step 2: $f$ is integral iff $f'$ is integral.
